docs.title: fastapi-passkeys
docs.text:
Passkeys / WebAuthn authentication for FastAPI — secure by default, storage-agnostic, async-native.

fastapi-passkeys owns the hard, security-sensitive part of passkeys — the WebAuthn ceremony, challenge integrity, signature-counter clone detection, and credential lifecycle — and stays out of the way of your idea of a session.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Verifies WebAuthn registration (attestation) and authentication (assertion) responses.
  • Generates and validates single-use, TTL-bound challenges.
  • Stores credentials through an async repository you choose (or implement).
  • Detects cloned authenticators via the signature counter.
  • Hands you the verified user and lets you mint whatever session/token you like.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
• It is not a session or JWT framework. You decide what "logged in" means.
  • It is not a FIDO2/CTAP client or a hardware-key management suite.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
• Quickstart — running in under 30 lines.
  • Concepts — a short, correct WebAuthn primer.
  • Storage backends — SQLAlchemy, Redis, and your own.
  • Security model — exactly what is and isn't protected.

docs.title: 0.2.0 audit report
docs.text:
The audit for the 0.2.0 release had three parts:

  1. Every issue and bug-related pull request in mkalioby/django-passkeys was mapped to the matching concern in fastapi-passkeys.
  2. Every line of this code base was reviewed, and its behaviour was checked against the WebAuthn Level 3 specification and py_webauthn 2.0–3.0.
  3. Comparable libraries were surveyed: py_webauthn, python-fido2, go-webauthn, SimpleWebAuthn, webauthn4j, java-webauthn-server, fido2-net-lib, webauthn-rs and Laragear/WebAuthn.

A finding was only marked Fixed after a regression test reproduced the failure against 0.1.2 and then passed. Those tests are in tests/test_regressions.py, tests/test_api_regressions.py, tests/test_features.py and tests/test_edge_cases.py.

Status legend:

  • Fixed: the defect was in 0.1.2 and is fixed in 0.2.0.
  • N/A: the architecture rules it out.
  • Already handled: 0.1.2 was already correct.
  • Docs: the concern is the integrator's to handle, and is now documented.
  • Deferred: accepted for now and put on the roadmap.

docs.title: A. Defects found in fastapi-passkeys 0.1.2
docs.text: ID Severity Finding Root cause Resolution F1 High userHandle was never checked. A usernameless assertion was accepted with any user handle, or none. The service looked credentials up by id only. WebAuthn §7.2 step 6 also requires the user handle to identify the credential's owner. Fixed. The handle is required in usernameless flows and must match whenever it is present. verify_user_handle is an opt-out for imported credentials. F2 High Registration hijack: register/finish did not check who was calling. Anyone holding another user's state handle could attach their own authenticator to that account. The handle was the only binding. The stateless store makes this worse, because a handle stays valid for the whole TTL even after use (F3). Fixed. RegistrationService.finish(user=...) rejects a handle issued to a different user. The router always passes the authenticated user. F3 High With the stateless store, a captured {state, credential} pair could be replayed to sign in again within challenge_ttl (5 min). The docs claimed the signature counter would stop a replay. Synced passkeys always report a counter of 0, so the counter check passes. Fixed. The store now keeps a per-process record of consumed tokens. It never evicts a record that has not expired: when full, it rejects new tokens (fail closed). The docs now state plainly that this does not cover several instances; use Redis there. F4 Medium InMemoryChallengeStore grew without bound. Each unauthenticated begin call added a challenge that was never removed, which is a memory DoS. Entries were only removed when a challenge was consumed. Fixed. Expired entries are evicted on put, and live entries are capped by max_entries. F5 Medium A configured origin such as https://example.com/ (trailing slash), https://Example.com or …:443 never matched, so every ceremony failed. Origins were compared as raw strings, but browsers serialize them in a normalized form. Fixed. Origins are normalized at startup. Origins outside rp_id, an rp_id that contains a scheme or port, and a TTL ≤ 0 are now rejected at startup. Android apk-key-hash origins are now accepted. F6 Medium Rename and delete returned 204 for unknown ids and for other users' ids. Delete still wrote a CREDENTIAL_REVOKED audit event, so the audit trail recorded revocations that never happened. The router delegated straight to the user-scoped repository write and never checked the result. Fixed. The router looks the credential up first. Unknown and foreign ids both return 404 (credential_not_found), and the audit event is emitted only on a real change. F6b Low Request bodies were unbounded: device name, state and userId. A long device name raised a database error (500) on PostgreSQL's String(255) column. Control characters were stored as-is. No length bounds on the schemas. Fixed. Device names are limited to 64 characters, trimmed, and may not contain control or format characters. state and userId are length-bounded. F7a Medium InMemoryCredentialRepository.add silently overwrote an existing credential id. In SQLAlchemy, a concurrent duplicate raised IntegrityError (500). add was not atomic, and the contract suite did not test duplicates. Fixed. Both adapters raise CredentialAlreadyExists (409). The contract suite now requires this. F7b Medium A PasskeyUser.id over 64 bytes, or an empty one, produced invalid options. An empty displayName breaks 1Password. No validation. Fixed. begin raises ConfigurationError for an id outside 1–64 bytes or an empty name. An empty display_name falls back to name. F7c Low Base64url decoding accepted non-canonical input: +, /, and any non-alphabet character, which was silently dropped. The stdlib urlsafe_b64decode is lenient. Fixed. Decoding is now strict. F7d Medium An audit sink that raised turned a completed ceremony into a 500. For example, the credential was stored but the client saw an error. Audit events were emitted inline, with no isolation. Fixed. emit_safely logs sink failures and continues. F7e Low is_discoverable was inferred from config, so it was wrong under resident_key=preferred. The credProps extension was neither requested nor read. Fixed. credProps is requested and stored, with config as the fallback. F7f Low BE/BS were captured only at registration. BS went stale, and a change to BE went undetected. The authentication path ignored the backup flags. Fixed. A BE change is rejected (enforce_backup_eligibility). BS is persisted on each login and reported in detail. F7g Medium With py_webauthn 2.0–2.4, detail["user_verified"] reported the policy rather than the authenticator's actual UV flag. It fell back to config.require_user_verification whenever the result had no user_verified field. Fixed. The UV bit is read from the verified authenticatorData. F7h Low SQLAlchemy failed to load a row containing a transport it did not know, which broke sign-in for that row. The BLOB primary key also made create_all fail on MySQL. Strict enum parsing; an unbounded LargeBinary primary key. Fixed. Unknown transports are skipped, smart-card was added, and the key is VARBINARY(1023) on MySQL. F7i Low FLAG_DISABLE deleted the credential without emitting CREDENTIAL_REVOKED. Missing event. Fixed. F8a Medium The dependency webauthn>=2.0 had no upper bound, and CI only tested the latest version. The declared floors (webauthn 2.0, FastAPI 0.110, pydantic 2.5) had never been tested. Testing them found F7g and a pydantic 2.5 bug where the name validators were skipped. Missing CI job. Fixed. The bound is now webauthn>=2.0,<4. CI adds a minimum-dependencies job and Python 3.14, and has been verified on webauthn 3.0.1. F8b Medium The release workflow published to PyPI on every push to main without running tests. The release job had no dependency on CI. Fixed. Release now needs: the full CI matrix, and major_on_zero = false stops an accidental 1.0. F9 High (docs) The quickstart and README said to build get_user from "an email from the request body". An app that followed this would let anyone register a passkey on anyone's account. Unsafe example. Fixed. The examples now resolve the authenticated user, and the security model explains why.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: A short primer on the WebAuthn vocabulary you'll meet in this library.

docs.title: Relying Party (RP)
docs.text: Your application. Identified by an RP ID (a registrable domain like example.com) and a human-readable RP name. Credentials are scoped to the RP ID, and the browser refuses to use a credential on a different origin — this is what makes passkeys phishing-resistant.

docs.title: Ceremonies
docs.text:
Two of them, each a begin → finish pair:

  • Registration (attestation): the authenticator creates a new key pair and returns the public key. You store it.
  • Authentication (assertion): the authenticator signs a fresh challenge with the private key. You verify the signature against the stored public key.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: A random value the server issues at begin and must see signed back at finish. It prevents replay. In this library it is single-use (in the in-memory and Redis stores) and expires after challenge_ttl. The client carries it between calls as an opaque state handle.

docs.title: Signature counter (sign_count)
docs.text: Many authenticators maintain a counter that increments on every assertion. If a presented counter does not exceed the stored one, the credential may have been cloned. This library stores and enforces the counter — see the security model.

docs.title: User verification (UV)
docs.text: Whether the authenticator proved the user's presence and identity (PIN/biometric) versus mere presence (a tap). Controlled by user_verification in the config.

docs.title: Discoverable credentials (resident keys)
docs.text: Credentials the authenticator can find without being told which user — this enables usernameless login (call authenticate/begin with no userId). Controlled by resident_key.

docs.title: Backup flags (BE / BS)
docs.text: Every response carries two bits. Backup eligible (BE) says the credential can be synced (a multi-device passkey); it is fixed for the credential's lifetime, so this library rejects an assertion that flips it. Backup state (BS) says it is currently backed up; it may change, and the library records the latest value on each sign-in. Use them for policy — e.g. nudge users whose only passkey is single-device (backupEligible: false) to add a second one.

docs.title: User handle
docs.text: PasskeyUser.id, UTF-8 encoded, is the WebAuthn user handle. The authenticator stores it with the credential and returns it on every discoverable sign-in. The library checks that it identifies the credential's owner. Keep it opaque (a UUID) and stable: it must not contain personal data, and it cannot be changed on credentials that already exist.

docs.title: Hints, autofill, signals and related origins (WebAuthn Level 3)
docs.text:
• Hints (PasskeyConfig.hints) nudge the browser toward a security key, the local device, or a phone.
  • Conditional mediation (autofill) shows passkeys in the username field's autofill menu. It is a usernameless authenticate/begin plus mediation: "conditional" on the client.
  • Signal API keeps passkey providers in sync with your server: tell them a credential was deleted, which credentials are still valid, or that the user's name changed.
  • Related origins let one rp_id serve several domains (e.g. example.com and example.co.uk) via /.well-known/webauthn.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
PasskeyConfig is a pydantic-settings model: pass values in code, or set PASSKEYS_<FIELD> environment variables (lists as JSON, e.g. PASSKEYS_EXPECTED_ORIGINS='["https://example.com"]').

The config is validated at startup, so mistakes that would otherwise fail every ceremony at runtime fail at startup instead.

docs.title: Relying party
docs.text:
Field Default Notes rp_id — Bare registrable domain: example.com. No scheme, port or path. Lowercased. rp_name — Shown by some authenticators. expected_origins — Exact origins allowed at verification. Normalized to the browser's form (https://Example.com:443/ → https://example.com). Every web origin must be rp_id or a subdomain of it. Android app origins (android:apk-key-hash:…) are accepted verbatim. related_origins [] Related Origin Requests: origins on other domains allowed to use rp_id. Served from /.well-known/webauthn by passkeys.well_known_router and accepted at verification. Browsers limit this to 5 distinct registrable domains.

Local development

rp_id="localhost" with expected_origins=["http://localhost:8000"]. Use localhost, not 127.0.0.1: an IP address is never a valid RP ID.

docs.title: Ceremony policy
docs.text: Field Default Notes user_verification preferred required makes the server reject assertions/attestations without the UV flag. Recommended for passwordless sign-in. resident_key preferred Discoverable credentials enable usernameless login and autofill. authenticator_attachment None platform / cross-platform to restrict; None allows both (and phones via hybrid). attestation none See the security model before asking for direct. hints [] WebAuthn L3 hints (security-key, client-device, hybrid), most preferred first. Sent with both ceremonies. timeout_ms 60000 Client-side hint. challenge_ttl 5 min Server-enforced. Must be positive; a warning is emitted if shorter than timeout_ms. max_credentials_per_user None Refuse registration beyond this many passkeys (credential_limit_reached, 409).

docs.title: Verification strictness
docs.text: Field Default Notes sign_count_policy strict-reject strict-reject, flag-disable, or audit-only — see clone detection. verify_user_handle True Require the assertion's userHandle to identify the credential owner. Turn off only for credentials imported from a library with a different user-handle scheme (migration). enforce_backup_eligibility True Reject an assertion whose BE flag differs from registration. Turn off if you imported credentials without knowing their BE flag.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Field Default Notes signing_secret None When set and no challenge_store is passed, Passkeys uses StatelessChallengeStore. Read its tradeoff first.

docs.title: Migrating from django-passkeys
docs.text: fastapi-passkeys is a redesign, not a port, so this is a concept map rather than a drop-in replacement. The data model is intentionally richer.

docs.title: Concept mapping
docs.text: django-passkeys fastapi-passkeys PasskeyModelBackend (auth backend) No backend — on_authenticated hook returns the verified user; you issue the session. UserPasskey model Credential domain entity + your chosen CredentialRepository. token (consolidated credential) Explicit public_key, transports, aaguid, backup_eligible, backup_state. (no signature counter) sign_count stored and enforced for clone detection. enabled flag / toggle No soft-disable yet: delete the credential, or use sign_count_policy="flag-disable". user-agent platform detection aaguid (authenticator model) and authenticatorAttachment in the result detail. FIDO_SERVER_ID callable (multi-tenant) Build a PasskeyConfig per tenant from an allow-list; never from the raw Host header. request.session['fido2_state'] Pluggable ChallengeStore (stateless, in-memory, or Redis) — no server session required. FIDO_SERVER_ID / FIDO_SERVER_NAME PasskeyConfig(rp_id=..., rp_name=...). KEY_ATTACHMENT PasskeyConfig(authenticator_attachment=...). DRF views Passkeys.router (FastAPI) or the services directly.

docs.title: Key behavioural differences
docs.text:
• Signature counter. django-passkeys stores no counter and cannot detect cloned authenticators. Here it is enforced by default (sign_count_policy="strict-reject"). If you import legacy credentials with no counter, start them at 0.
  • Challenges are not in the session. The client carries an opaque state handle between begin and finish, so the flow works for stateless SPAs and mobile clients.
  • Auth is decoupled. The library verifies the passkey and stops there; minting a session or JWT is your code in on_authenticated.

docs.title: Importing existing credentials
docs.text:
Map each UserPasskey row into a Credential: decode the stored credential id to bytes, set public_key from your stored COSE key, and set sign_count=0. Persist via your repository's add. Keep the same rp_id — credentials are bound to it and cannot be moved.

Two things differ from what django-passkeys stored, and both matter for imported keys:

  • User handle. django-passkeys put base64url(username) in the WebAuthn user handle; this library uses PasskeyUser.id and verifies that the assertion's userHandle matches the credential owner. Authenticators keep the handle they were given at registration, so imported passkeys will present the old one. Set verify_user_handle=False while you still have imported credentials. Ownership is still enforced by credential-id lookup and the signature; you only lose the extra userHandle cross-check.
  • Backup eligibility. django-passkeys did not record the BE flag. If you import with backup_eligible=False, synced passkeys (which report BE=1) would be rejected. Either set enforce_backup_eligibility=False for the transition, or set backup_eligible=True for keys you know are synced.

Ask users to register a fresh passkey after migrating; you can turn both settings back on once the imported credentials have been replaced.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install fastapi-passkeys

docs.title: Wire it up
docs.text:
You provide two hooks and a storage backend; the library provides the router.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi_passkeys import Passkeys, PasskeyConfig, PasskeyUser, AuthenticationResult
from fastapi_passkeys.contrib import InMemoryCredentialRepository


async def get_user(request: Request) -> PasskeyUser:
    # Return the *authenticated* user — from your session or a verified sign-up
    # token. Never trust an email/user id sent by the client: whoever this
    # returns is who the new passkey is attached to.
    account = await current_account(request)  # your auth; raise HTTPException(401) if none
    return PasskeyUser(
        id=account.passkey_id,          # opaque, stable, 1-64 bytes (e.g. a UUID) — not an email
        name=account.email,             # shown in the passkey picker
        display_name=account.full_name,
    )


async def on_authenticated(request: Request, result: AuthenticationResult) -> dict:
    # The passkey is verified. Now mint *your* session or token.
    return {"access_token": issue_token(result.user_id)}


passkeys = Passkeys(
    config=PasskeyConfig(
        rp_id="example.com",
        rp_name="Example",
        expected_origins=["https://example.com"],
    ),
    credential_repository=InMemoryCredentialRepository(),
    get_user=get_user,
    on_authenticated=on_authenticated,
)

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(passkeys.router, prefix="/auth/passkeys")
passkeys.install_exception_handlers(app)

docs.title: The two round-trips
docs.text:
Each ceremony is begin then finish. begin returns the options your frontend passes to navigator.credentials.create() / .get(), plus an opaque state handle. Echo that state back to finish alongside the authenticator's response. The challenge is single-use and TTL-bound — no server session is required between the calls.

POST /auth/passkeys/register/begin      -> { publicKey, state }
POST /auth/passkeys/register/finish     <- { credential, state, deviceName? }

POST /auth/passkeys/authenticate/begin  -> { publicKey, state }
POST /auth/passkeys/authenticate/finish <- { credential, state }

register/finish and the credential-management endpoints call get_user again, so the ceremony stays bound to the user who started it.

Running more than one worker?

The default challenge store is in-memory and per-process. With uvicorn --workers 4 (or several pods), begin and finish can hit different processes and fail with challenge_not_found. Pass challenge_store=RedisChallengeStore(...).

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
Use the browser's JSON helpers where available — PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON(begin.publicKey) / parseRequestOptionsFromJSON(...) and credential.toJSON() — and fall back to manual base64url conversion elsewhere. If you convert by hand, handle Uint8Array as well as ArrayBuffer (some password managers return typed arrays).

The wire format the finish endpoints expect is the standard WebAuthn JSON encoding:

{
  "state": "<from begin>",
  "credential": {
    "id": "<base64url>", "rawId": "<base64url>", "type": "public-key",
    "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
    "clientExtensionResults": {"credProps": {"rk": true}},
    "response": {
      "clientDataJSON": "<base64url>",
      "attestationObject": "<base64url, registration>",
      "transports": ["internal", "hybrid"],
      "authenticatorData": "<base64url, authentication>",
      "signature": "<base64url, authentication>",
      "userHandle": "<base64url or null, authentication>"
    }
  }
}

Autofill (conditional UI): add autocomplete="username webauthn" to your username field and call authenticate/begin with no userId, then navigator.credentials.get({publicKey, mediation: "conditional", signal}). Abort that request (AbortController) before starting a modal one — browsers allow only one pending WebAuthn request.

Signal API: when authenticate/finish fails with credential_not_found, the error body carries error.signal.unknownCredential; pass it to PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential() so the passkey provider forgets a credential you deleted. GET /credentials/signals returns ready-made payloads for signalAllAcceptedCredentials() and signalCurrentUserDetails().

class Passkeys:
    """High-level entry point wiring config, storage, engine, and HTTP routes."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        config: PasskeyConfig,
        credential_repository: CredentialRepository,
        challenge_store: ChallengeStore | None = None,
        get_user: GetUser | None = None,
        on_authenticated: OnAuthenticated | None = None,
        engine: WebAuthnEngine | None = None,
        audit: AuditSink | None = None,
        clock: Clock | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self._clock = clock or SystemClock()
        self._audit = audit or NullAuditSink()
        self._engine = engine or PyWebAuthnEngine()
        self._credentials = credential_repository
        self._challenges = challenge_store or self._default_store(config, self._clock)
        self._get_user = get_user
        self._on_authenticated = on_authenticated

        self.registration = RegistrationService(
            config=config,
            credentials=self._credentials,
            challenges=self._challenges,
            engine=self._engine,
            clock=self._clock,
            audit=self._audit,
        )
        self.authentication = AuthenticationService(
            config=config,
            credentials=self._credentials,
            challenges=self._challenges,
            engine=self._engine,
            clock=self._clock,
            audit=self._audit,
        )
        self.router = self._build_router()

    @staticmethod
    def _default_store(config: PasskeyConfig, clock: Clock) -> ChallengeStore:
        if config.signing_secret is not None:
            return StatelessChallengeStore(config.signing_secret.get_secret_value(), clock=clock)
        return InMemoryChallengeStore(clock=clock)

    def install_exception_handlers(self, app: FastAPI) -> None:
        """Register JSON error responses for the library's exceptions."""
        install_exception_handlers(app)

    @property
    def well_known_router(self) -> APIRouter:
        """Serves ``/.well-known/webauthn`` for WebAuthn Related Origin Requests.

        Mount it **without a prefix** on the app served at ``rp_id``::

            app.include_router(passkeys.well_known_router)

        Responds 404 unless ``config.related_origins`` is set.
        """
        router = APIRouter()

        @router.get("/.well-known/webauthn", include_in_schema=False)
        async def related_origins() -> dict[str, list[str]]:
            if not self.config.related_origins:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=404)
            origins = [o for o in self.config.allowed_origins if o.startswith("http")]
            return {"origins": origins}

        return router

    def _build_router(self) -> APIRouter:
        router = APIRouter(tags=["passkeys"])

        @router.post("/register/begin", response_model=BeginResponse)
        async def register_begin(request: Request) -> BeginResponse:
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            options, handle = await self.registration.begin(user)
            return BeginResponse(publicKey=options, state=handle)

        @router.post("/register/finish", response_model=RegisterFinishResponse)
        async def register_finish(
            body: RegisterFinishRequest, request: Request
        ) -> RegisterFinishResponse:
            # Bind the ceremony to the caller: a handle issued to another user is
            # rejected, so a leaked handle cannot attach an attacker's key.
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            credential = await self.registration.finish(
                response=body.credential,
                handle=body.state,
                device_name=body.device_name,
                user=user,
            )
            return RegisterFinishResponse(credentialId=bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id))

        @router.post("/authenticate/begin", response_model=BeginResponse)
        async def authenticate_begin(body: AuthBeginRequest | None = None) -> BeginResponse:
            options, handle = await self.authentication.begin(
                user_id=body.user_id if body else None
            )
            return BeginResponse(publicKey=options, state=handle)

        @router.post("/authenticate/finish")
        async def authenticate_finish(body: AuthFinishRequest, request: Request) -> Any:
            result = await self.authentication.finish(response=body.credential, handle=body.state)
            if self._on_authenticated is not None:
                return await maybe_await(self._on_authenticated(request, result))
            return {"status": "ok", "userId": result.user_id}

        @router.get("/credentials", response_model=list[CredentialView])
        async def list_credentials(request: Request) -> list[CredentialView]:
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            credentials = await self._credentials.list_by_user(user.id)
            return [CredentialView.from_domain(c) for c in credentials]

        @router.get("/credentials/signals", response_model=SignalsResponse)
        async def credential_signals(request: Request) -> SignalsResponse:
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            credentials = await self._credentials.list_by_user(user.id)
            user_id = bytes_to_b64url(user_handle(user.id))
            return SignalsResponse(
                allAcceptedCredentials={
                    "rpId": self.config.rp_id,
                    "userId": user_id,
                    "allAcceptedCredentialIds": [
                        bytes_to_b64url(c.credential_id) for c in credentials
                    ],
                },
                currentUserDetails={
                    "rpId": self.config.rp_id,
                    "userId": user_id,
                    "name": user.name,
                    "displayName": user.display_name or user.name,
                },
            )

        @router.patch("/credentials/{credential_id}", status_code=204)
        async def rename_credential(
            credential_id: str, body: RenameRequest, request: Request
        ) -> Response:
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            credential = await self._owned_credential(credential_id, user.id)
            await self._credentials.rename(credential.credential_id, user.id, body.device_name)
            await self._emit(AuditEventType.CREDENTIAL_RENAMED, user.id, credential)
            return Response(status_code=204)

        @router.delete("/credentials/{credential_id}", status_code=204)
        async def delete_credential(credential_id: str, request: Request) -> Response:
            user = await resolve_user(self._get_user, request)
            credential = await self._owned_credential(credential_id, user.id)
            await self._credentials.delete(credential.credential_id, user.id)
            await self._emit(AuditEventType.CREDENTIAL_REVOKED, user.id, credential)
            return Response(status_code=204)

        return router

    async def _owned_credential(self, credential_id: str, user_id: str) -> Credential:
        """Resolve a credential the caller owns, or 404 — identically for "absent"
        and "someone else's", so ids cannot be probed across accounts."""
        try:
            raw = b64url_to_bytes(credential_id)
        except ValueError:
            raise ManagedCredentialNotFound() from None
        credential = await self._credentials.get_by_credential_id(raw)
        if credential is None or credential.user_id != user_id:
            raise ManagedCredentialNotFound()
        return credential

    async def _emit(self, kind: AuditEventType, user_id: str, credential: Credential) -> None:
        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(
                type=kind,
                timestamp=self._clock.now(),
                user_id=user_id,
                credential_id=bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id),
            ),
        )

class PasskeyConfig(BaseSettings):
    """Relying-party policy for passkey ceremonies."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="PASSKEYS_", extra="ignore")

    rp_id: str = Field(
        description="Relying Party ID — a bare registrable domain such as 'example.com' "
        "(no scheme, port or path). Every web origin must be this domain or a subdomain.",
    )
    rp_name: str = Field(description="Human-readable RP name shown by authenticators.")
    expected_origins: list[str] = Field(
        description="Allowed origins, e.g. ['https://example.com']. Normalized to the "
        "browser's serialization. Android app origins ('android:apk-key-hash:...') are "
        "accepted verbatim.",
    )

    challenge_ttl: timedelta = Field(
        default=timedelta(seconds=300),
        description="Server-enforced challenge lifetime, independent of the client timeout.",
    )
    timeout_ms: int = Field(
        default=60_000,
        ge=1_000,
        description="Client-side ceremony timeout hint passed to the authenticator.",
    )

    user_verification: UserVerification = UserVerification.PREFERRED
    attestation: AttestationPreference = AttestationPreference.NONE
    authenticator_attachment: AuthenticatorAttachment | None = None
    resident_key: ResidentKeyRequirement = ResidentKeyRequirement.PREFERRED
    sign_count_policy: SignCountPolicy = SignCountPolicy.STRICT_REJECT

    hints: list[Hint] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="WebAuthn L3 hints sent with both ceremonies, most preferred first.",
    )
    max_credentials_per_user: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=1,
        description="Refuse to register more passkeys than this per user. None = no limit.",
    )
    verify_user_handle: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Require the assertion's userHandle to identify the credential's owner "
        "(WebAuthn §7.2 step 6). Disable only for credentials imported from a library that "
        "used a different user-handle scheme.",
    )
    enforce_backup_eligibility: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Reject an assertion whose backup-eligible (BE) flag differs from the one "
        "recorded at registration; BE is fixed for a credential's lifetime.",
    )
    related_origins: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="WebAuthn Related Origin Requests: extra web origins (on other domains) "
        "allowed to use this rp_id. Served from /.well-known/webauthn and accepted at verify.",
    )

    signing_secret: SecretStr | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="HMAC secret for the stateless challenge store. Required only when used.",
    )

    @field_validator("rp_id")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_rp_id(cls, value: str) -> str:
        rp_id = value.strip().lower().rstrip(".")
        if not rp_id or any(c in rp_id for c in ":/?#@ \t") or rp_id.startswith("."):
            raise ValueError(
                f"rp_id must be a bare domain such as 'example.com' (no scheme, port or "
                f"path), got {value!r}"
            )
        return rp_id

    @field_validator("expected_origins")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_origins(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        if not value:
            raise ValueError("expected_origins must contain at least one origin")
        normalized: list[str] = []
        for origin in value:
            item = _normalize_origin(origin)
            if item not in normalized:
                normalized.append(item)
        return normalized

    @field_validator("related_origins")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_related_origins(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        normalized: list[str] = []
        for origin in value:
            item = _normalize_origin(origin)
            if item.startswith(_ANDROID_ORIGIN_PREFIX):
                raise ValueError("related_origins must be web origins (http/https)")
            if item not in normalized:
                normalized.append(item)
        return normalized

    @field_validator("challenge_ttl")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_ttl(cls, value: timedelta) -> timedelta:
        if value <= timedelta(0):
            raise ValueError("challenge_ttl must be positive")
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_origins_match_rp_id(self) -> PasskeyConfig:
        for origin in self.expected_origins:
            if origin.startswith(_ANDROID_ORIGIN_PREFIX):
                continue
            host = urlsplit(origin).hostname or ""
            if host != self.rp_id and not host.endswith("." + self.rp_id):
                # Browsers refuse such a pairing ("The RP ID is not a registrable
                # domain suffix of the origin"), so fail at startup, not at runtime.
                raise ValueError(
                    f"origin {origin!r} is not on rp_id {self.rp_id!r} or one of its subdomains"
                )
        if self.challenge_ttl < timedelta(milliseconds=self.timeout_ms):
            warnings.warn(
                "challenge_ttl is shorter than timeout_ms: a user who takes the full "
                "client timeout will find the challenge already expired.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return self

    @property
    def allowed_origins(self) -> list[str]:
        """Every origin accepted at verification: ``expected_origins`` + ``related_origins``."""
        return self.expected_origins + [
            o for o in self.related_origins if o not in self.expected_origins
        ]

    @property
    def require_user_verification(self) -> bool:
        """Whether assertions/attestations must prove user verification."""
        return self.user_verification is UserVerification.REQUIRED

class RegistrationService:
    """Begins and finishes passkey registration (attestation) ceremonies."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        config: PasskeyConfig,
        credentials: CredentialRepository,
        challenges: ChallengeStore,
        engine: WebAuthnEngine,
        clock: Clock | None = None,
        audit: AuditSink | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._credentials = credentials
        self._challenges = challenges
        self._engine = engine
        self._clock = clock or SystemClock()
        self._audit = audit or NullAuditSink()

    async def begin(self, user: PasskeyUser) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
        """Issue creation options and a challenge handle the client echoes back."""
        user = _validated(user)
        existing = await self._credentials.list_by_user(user.id)
        self._check_limit(existing)
        challenge = secrets.token_bytes(_CHALLENGE_BYTES)
        now = self._clock.now()
        options = self._engine.registration_options(
            config=self._config, user=user, challenge=challenge, exclude=existing
        )
        handle = await self._challenges.put(
            RegistrationChallenge(
                challenge=challenge,
                user=user,
                created_at=now,
                expires_at=now + self._config.challenge_ttl,
            )
        )
        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(type=AuditEventType.REGISTRATION_BEGAN, timestamp=now, user_id=user.id),
        )
        return options, handle

    async def finish(
        self,
        *,
        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
        handle: str,
        device_name: str = "",
        user: PasskeyUser | None = None,
    ) -> Credential:
        """Verify the attestation response and persist the new credential.

        Pass ``user`` — the user authenticated on *this* request — to bind the
        ceremony to them: a handle issued to someone else is rejected. The
        bundled router always does this. Without it, anyone holding a valid
        handle can attach their own authenticator to the account it was issued
        for.
        """
        stored = await self._challenges.consume(handle)
        if not isinstance(stored, RegistrationChallenge):
            await self._fail(AuditEventType.CHALLENGE_EXPIRED, user_id=None)
            raise ChallengeNotFound()

        try:
            if user is not None and user.id != stored.user.id:
                raise RegistrationUserMismatch()
            verified = self._engine.verify_registration(
                config=self._config, response=response, expected_challenge=stored.challenge
            )
            if await self._credentials.get_by_credential_id(verified.credential_id) is not None:
                raise CredentialAlreadyExists()
            self._check_limit(await self._credentials.list_by_user(stored.user.id))

            now = self._clock.now()
            discoverable = verified.is_discoverable
            if discoverable is None:  # client did not report credProps
                discoverable = self._config.resident_key is ResidentKeyRequirement.REQUIRED
            credential = Credential(
                credential_id=verified.credential_id,
                user_id=stored.user.id,
                public_key=verified.public_key,
                sign_count=verified.sign_count,
                transports=verified.transports,
                aaguid=verified.aaguid,
                backup_eligible=verified.backup_eligible,
                backup_state=verified.backup_state,
                device_name=device_name,
                is_discoverable=discoverable,
                attestation_fmt=verified.attestation_fmt,
                created_at=now,
                last_used_at=None,
            )
            # Repositories raise CredentialAlreadyExists on a concurrent duplicate.
            await self._credentials.add(credential)
        except PasskeyError as exc:
            await self._fail(
                AuditEventType.REGISTRATION_FAILED, user_id=stored.user.id, reason=exc.code
            )
            raise

        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(
                type=AuditEventType.REGISTRATION_SUCCEEDED,
                timestamp=now,
                user_id=stored.user.id,
                credential_id=bytes_to_b64url(verified.credential_id),
            ),
        )
        return credential

    def _check_limit(self, existing: list[Credential]) -> None:
        limit = self._config.max_credentials_per_user
        if limit is not None and len(existing) >= limit:
            raise CredentialLimitReached()

    async def _fail(
        self, event_type: AuditEventType, *, user_id: str | None, reason: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(
                type=event_type,
                timestamp=self._clock.now(),
                user_id=user_id,
                detail={"reason": reason} if reason else {},
            ),
        )

class AuthenticationService:
    """Begins and finishes passkey authentication (assertion) ceremonies."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        config: PasskeyConfig,
        credentials: CredentialRepository,
        challenges: ChallengeStore,
        engine: WebAuthnEngine,
        clock: Clock | None = None,
        audit: AuditSink | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._credentials = credentials
        self._challenges = challenges
        self._engine = engine
        self._clock = clock or SystemClock()
        self._audit = audit or NullAuditSink()
        # Repositories written against 0.1 have no ``backup_state`` parameter.
        self._persist_backup_state = _accepts_kwarg(credentials.update_usage, "backup_state")

    async def begin(self, *, user_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
        """Issue request options and a challenge handle.

        Pass ``user_id`` for a username-first flow (restricts allowed credentials)
        or omit it for a usernameless / discoverable-credential flow.
        """
        user_id = user_id or None
        allow = await self._credentials.list_by_user(user_id) if user_id else []
        challenge = secrets.token_bytes(_CHALLENGE_BYTES)
        now = self._clock.now()
        options = self._engine.authentication_options(
            config=self._config, challenge=challenge, allow=allow
        )
        handle = await self._challenges.put(
            AuthenticationChallenge(
                challenge=challenge,
                user_id=user_id,
                created_at=now,
                expires_at=now + self._config.challenge_ttl,
            )
        )
        await self._emit(AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_BEGAN, user_id=user_id)
        return options, handle

    async def finish(self, *, response: dict[str, Any] | str, handle: str) -> AuthenticationResult:
        """Verify the assertion, enforce the signature counter, and record usage."""
        stored = await self._challenges.consume(handle)
        if not isinstance(stored, AuthenticationChallenge):
            await self._emit(AuditEventType.CHALLENGE_EXPIRED)
            raise ChallengeNotFound()

        data = _as_dict(response)
        credential = await self._resolve_credential(data, stored)
        cred_b64 = bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id)

        try:
            verified = self._engine.verify_authentication(
                config=self._config,
                response=response,
                expected_challenge=stored.challenge,
                credential=credential,
            )
            if verified.credential_id != credential.credential_id:
                raise AssertionVerificationError()
            self._check_backup_eligibility(credential, verified)
        except PasskeyError as exc:
            await self._emit(
                AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED,
                user_id=credential.user_id,
                credential_id=cred_b64,
                reason=exc.code,
            )
            raise

        await self._enforce_sign_count(credential, verified)

        now = self._clock.now()
        backup_state = (
            verified.backup_state if verified.backup_state is not None else credential.backup_state
        )
        if self._persist_backup_state:
            await self._credentials.update_usage(
                credential.credential_id,
                sign_count=verified.new_sign_count,
                last_used_at=now,
                backup_state=backup_state,
            )
        else:
            await self._credentials.update_usage(
                credential.credential_id, sign_count=verified.new_sign_count, last_used_at=now
            )
        await self._emit(
            AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_SUCCEEDED,
            user_id=credential.user_id,
            credential_id=cred_b64,
        )
        updated = dataclasses.replace(
            credential,
            sign_count=verified.new_sign_count,
            last_used_at=now,
            backup_state=backup_state,
        )
        attachment = data.get("authenticatorAttachment")
        return AuthenticationResult(
            user_id=credential.user_id,
            credential=updated,
            detail={
                "user_verified": verified.user_verified,
                # Flags as presented by *this* assertion.
                "backup_eligible": (
                    verified.backup_eligible
                    if verified.backup_eligible is not None
                    else credential.backup_eligible
                ),
                "backup_state": backup_state,
                "authenticator_attachment": attachment if attachment in _ATTACHMENTS else None,
            },
        )

    async def _resolve_credential(
        self, data: dict[str, Any], stored: AuthenticationChallenge
    ) -> Credential:
        credential_id = _b64_field(data.get("rawId") or data.get("id"))
        credential = (
            await self._credentials.get_by_credential_id(credential_id) if credential_id else None
        )
        if credential is None:
            await self._emit(AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, user_id=stored.user_id)
            error = CredentialNotFound()
            if credential_id:
                # Lets the browser prune a passkey we no longer know about
                # (PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential).
                error.extra["signal"] = {
                    "unknownCredential": {
                        "rpId": self._config.rp_id,
                        "credentialId": bytes_to_b64url(credential_id),
                    }
                }
            raise error

        if not self._owner_matches(credential, data, stored):
            # Same generic error as "unknown" so we do not leak which check failed.
            await self._emit(
                AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED,
                user_id=stored.user_id,
                credential_id=bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id),
                reason="owner_mismatch",
            )
            raise CredentialNotFound()
        return credential

    def _owner_matches(
        self, credential: Credential, data: dict[str, Any], stored: AuthenticationChallenge
    ) -> bool:
        """WebAuthn §7.2 step 6: the credential must belong to the identified user."""
        if stored.user_id is not None and credential.user_id != stored.user_id:
            return False
        if not self._config.verify_user_handle:
            return True
        inner = data.get("response")
        raw_handle = inner.get("userHandle") if isinstance(inner, dict) else None
        if raw_handle is None:
            # Optional only when the user was identified before the ceremony.
            return stored.user_id is not None
        return _b64_field(raw_handle) == user_handle(credential.user_id)

    def _check_backup_eligibility(
        self, credential: Credential, verified: VerifiedAuthentication
    ) -> None:
        if (
            self._config.enforce_backup_eligibility
            and verified.backup_eligible is not None
            and verified.backup_eligible != credential.backup_eligible
        ):
            # BE is fixed for a credential's lifetime (WebAuthn §6.1.3); a change
            # means a different or misbehaving authenticator.
            raise AssertionVerificationError()

    async def _enforce_sign_count(
        self, credential: Credential, verified: VerifiedAuthentication
    ) -> None:
        old, new = credential.sign_count, verified.new_sign_count
        # Counter of 0 on both sides means the authenticator does not implement one.
        if new == 0 and old == 0:
            return
        if new > old:
            return
        cred_b64 = bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id)
        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(
                type=AuditEventType.CLONE_SUSPECTED,
                timestamp=self._clock.now(),
                user_id=credential.user_id,
                credential_id=cred_b64,
                detail={
                    "stored_sign_count": old,
                    "presented_sign_count": new,
                    "policy": self._config.sign_count_policy.value,
                },
            ),
        )
        policy = self._config.sign_count_policy
        if policy is SignCountPolicy.AUDIT_ONLY:
            return
        if policy is SignCountPolicy.FLAG_DISABLE:
            await self._credentials.delete(credential.credential_id, credential.user_id)
            await self._emit(
                AuditEventType.CREDENTIAL_REVOKED,
                user_id=credential.user_id,
                credential_id=cred_b64,
                reason="clone_suspected",
            )
        raise CloneDetectedError()

    async def _emit(
        self,
        event_type: AuditEventType,
        *,
        user_id: str | None = None,
        credential_id: str | None = None,
        reason: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        await emit_safely(
            self._audit,
            AuditEvent(
                type=event_type,
                timestamp=self._clock.now(),
                user_id=user_id,
                credential_id=credential_id,
                detail={"reason": reason} if reason else {},
            ),
        )

async def begin(self, *, user_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
    """Issue request options and a challenge handle.

    Pass ``user_id`` for a username-first flow (restricts allowed credentials)
    or omit it for a usernameless / discoverable-credential flow.
    """
    user_id = user_id or None
    allow = await self._credentials.list_by_user(user_id) if user_id else []
    challenge = secrets.token_bytes(_CHALLENGE_BYTES)
    now = self._clock.now()
    options = self._engine.authentication_options(
        config=self._config, challenge=challenge, allow=allow
    )
    handle = await self._challenges.put(
        AuthenticationChallenge(
            challenge=challenge,
            user_id=user_id,
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=now + self._config.challenge_ttl,
        )
    )
    await self._emit(AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_BEGAN, user_id=user_id)
    return options, handle

async def finish(self, *, response: dict[str, Any] | str, handle: str) -> AuthenticationResult:
    """Verify the assertion, enforce the signature counter, and record usage."""
    stored = await self._challenges.consume(handle)
    if not isinstance(stored, AuthenticationChallenge):
        await self._emit(AuditEventType.CHALLENGE_EXPIRED)
        raise ChallengeNotFound()

    data = _as_dict(response)
    credential = await self._resolve_credential(data, stored)
    cred_b64 = bytes_to_b64url(credential.credential_id)

    try:
        verified = self._engine.verify_authentication(
            config=self._config,
            response=response,
            expected_challenge=stored.challenge,
            credential=credential,
        )
        if verified.credential_id != credential.credential_id:
            raise AssertionVerificationError()
        self._check_backup_eligibility(credential, verified)
    except PasskeyError as exc:
        await self._emit(
            AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED,
            user_id=credential.user_id,
            credential_id=cred_b64,
            reason=exc.code,
        )
        raise

    await self._enforce_sign_count(credential, verified)

    now = self._clock.now()
    backup_state = (
        verified.backup_state if verified.backup_state is not None else credential.backup_state
    )
    if self._persist_backup_state:
        await self._credentials.update_usage(
            credential.credential_id,
            sign_count=verified.new_sign_count,
            last_used_at=now,
            backup_state=backup_state,
        )
    else:
        await self._credentials.update_usage(
            credential.credential_id, sign_count=verified.new_sign_count, last_used_at=now
        )
    await self._emit(
        AuditEventType.AUTHENTICATION_SUCCEEDED,
        user_id=credential.user_id,
        credential_id=cred_b64,
    )
    updated = dataclasses.replace(
        credential,
        sign_count=verified.new_sign_count,
        last_used_at=now,
        backup_state=backup_state,
    )
    attachment = data.get("authenticatorAttachment")
    return AuthenticationResult(
        user_id=credential.user_id,
        credential=updated,
        detail={
            "user_verified": verified.user_verified,
            # Flags as presented by *this* assertion.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: This library is responsible for the WebAuthn ceremony and credential integrity. It is not responsible for your session, rate limiting, or transport security — those are listed under your responsibility.

docs.title: What the library protects
docs.text: Concern How Challenge integrity CSPRNG (secrets.token_bytes), bound to user + ceremony type. Replay Single-use challenges: ChallengeStore.consume fetches and invalidates atomically. Challenge expiry TTL enforced server-side (challenge_ttl), independent of the client timeout. RP ID validation The authenticator data RP-ID hash is checked against rp_id. Origin validation Exact match against expected_origins (+ related_origins), normalized at startup to the browser's serialization; origins not on rp_id are rejected at startup. Registration hijack register/finish is bound to the user who called register/begin: a handle issued to someone else is rejected. Credential ownership The assertion's userHandle must identify the credential's owner (WebAuthn §7.2 step 6); a user-bound ceremony rejects anyone else's credential. Credential overwrite Repositories must refuse — not overwrite — a duplicate credential id (enforced by the contract suite). Cloned authenticators sign_count is stored and required to advance; a regression is audited and handled by sign_count_policy. Backup eligibility The BE flag is fixed per credential; an assertion that flips it is rejected (enforce_backup_eligibility). BS is tracked on every login. User verification Enforced when user_verification="required"; the actual UV flag is reported in AuthenticationResult.detail. Credential management Rename/delete are owner-scoped and return 404 both for unknown ids and for other users' ids (no existence oracle). Input bounds state, userId, and device names are length-bounded; device names reject control characters. Resource exhaustion The in-memory challenge store evicts expired entries and caps live ones (max_entries). Information leakage Verification failures use generic errors; audit events carry no secrets or keys. Broken audit sinks A sink that raises is logged and ignored; it never turns a completed ceremony into an error.

docs.title: Clone detection policy
docs.text:
When the signature counter fails to advance, the configured sign_count_policy applies:

  • strict-reject (default) — reject the attempt; the credential remains for investigation.
  • flag-disable — reject and delete the credential so it cannot be retried (also emits CREDENTIAL_REVOKED).
  • audit-only — accept, but emit CLONE_SUSPECTED. For apps where a false positive (a locked-out user) costs more than the residual risk.

All emit a CLONE_SUSPECTED audit event.

Counters and synced passkeys

iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager and most other synced passkey providers always report a counter of 0. For those credentials the counter can neither detect clones nor stop replays — single-use challenges are what protect you.

docs.title: Challenge store tradeoffs
docs.text:
Store Single-use Infra Notes InMemoryChallengeStore ✅ none Single process only — with several workers, begin and finish can land on different processes. RedisChallengeStore ✅ (atomic GETDEL) Redis Recommended for multi-instance deployments. StatelessChallengeStore ⚠️ per process none Signed token. Remembers consumed tokens in-process until they expire (failing closed when max_consumed live records are held), so a replay against the same process fails — but a captured {state, credential} pair can be replayed against another instance until the token expires.

Stateless store across several instances

Before 0.2 the stateless store relied on the signature counter to stop replays. That does not work for synced passkeys (counter always 0): a captured request body could be replayed to log in again within challenge_ttl. 0.2 adds the per-process guard above. If you run more than one instance, use RedisChallengeStore, or keep challenge_ttl short and make sure request bodies never reach logs or traces.

The per-process guard holds at most max_consumed (default 100,000) unexpired records. When it is full, the store fails closed: it refuses new ceremonies on that process until records expire, and logs a warning on fastapi_passkeys.stateless. That is a deliberate trade, a temporary lockout instead of re-opened replay. A client that can push that many finish requests within one challenge_ttl can therefore block sign-ins on an instance. Rate-limit the endpoints, or use Redis.

Passkeys picks the stateless store automatically when signing_secret is set and no challenge_store is passed.

docs.title: Your responsibility
docs.text:
• get_user must return the authenticated user. It decides whose account a new passkey is attached to and whose passkeys are listed, renamed, or deleted. Resolve it from your session or a verified sign-up token — never from an identifier the client sends (an email or user id in the body or query string), or anyone can add their passkey to anyone's account. Raise HTTPException(401) when there is no authenticated user.
  • Use an opaque PasskeyUser.id. It becomes the WebAuthn user handle, which the authenticator stores and may sync. Use a UUID or random id, not an email address (it must be 1–64 bytes).
  • Re-authenticate before sensitive changes. Consider requiring a recent sign-in ("sudo mode") before adding or deleting passkeys, so a stolen session cannot swap in an attacker's key. Add it as a dependency: app.include_router(passkeys.router, dependencies=[...]).
  • Sessions/tokens: you mint them in on_authenticated. Set Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies. If you use cookie sessions, the management endpoints are state-changing — keep CSRF protection in place (the JSON content type alone forces a CORS preflight, but do not rely on CORS misconfiguration never happening).
  • Rate limiting: the begin endpoints are unauthenticated. Put a limiter (reverse proxy, or e.g. slowapi) in front of */begin and */finish, per IP and per account.
  • Username enumeration: authenticate/begin with a userId returns that user's credential ids (allowCredentials), and an empty list reveals that a user has no passkeys. Prefer usernameless sign-in (no userId, discoverable credentials), or put that endpoint behind your own lookup that does not reveal whether an account exists. Likewise, whether a given credential id is registered can be told apart from the error code (credential_not_found vs assertion_verification_failed). Credential ids are not secrets, so this is by design: it lets the browser's Signal API prune deleted passkeys.
  • Multi-tenant rp_id: never derive rp_id or origins from the Host header unchecked — map the host through an allow-list of tenants.
  • Render names safely: device names are user input. Escape them (textContent, template auto-escaping) wherever you display them.
  • HTTPS: WebAuthn requires a secure context. http://localhost is the only exception.
  • Attestation: attestation="direct" asks for an attestation statement, and its signature is verified, but no trust roots or metadata (FIDO MDS) are checked. Do not treat it as proof of the authenticator model.
  • Changing rp_id orphans every credential. Credentials are bound to the RP ID forever.

docs.title: Storage backends
docs.text: The library never imports an ORM. Storage is two async Protocols: CredentialRepository (persistent passkeys) and ChallengeStore (in-flight challenges).

docs.title: Shipped adapters
docs.text:
# Core (no extras)
from fastapi_passkeys.contrib import (
    InMemoryCredentialRepository,
    InMemoryChallengeStore,
    StatelessChallengeStore,
)

docs.title: SQLAlchemy ([sqlalchemy])
docs.text:
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from fastapi_passkeys.contrib.sqlalchemy import PasskeyBase, SqlAlchemyCredentialRepository

engine = create_async_engine("postgresql+asyncpg://localhost/app")
async with engine.begin() as conn:
    await conn.run_sync(PasskeyBase.metadata.create_all)

repo = SqlAlchemyCredentialRepository(async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False))

user_id is a plain indexed string (the WebAuthn user handle). Add a foreign key to your users table in your own migration if you want referential integrity.

docs.title: Redis challenge store ([redis])
docs.text:
from redis.asyncio import Redis
from fastapi_passkeys.contrib.redis import RedisChallengeStore

store = RedisChallengeStore(Redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379/0"))

docs.title: Repository contract (0.2)
docs.text:
• add must raise CredentialAlreadyExists — never overwrite — when the credential id is already stored. Credential ids are chosen by the authenticator, so an overwrite would let a user replace someone else's passkey. The contract suite checks this. Back it with a unique / primary key and translate the integrity error, as the SQLAlchemy adapter does.
  • update_usage accepts an optional backup_state: bool | None keyword (the credential's current BS flag; None = unchanged). Repositories written for 0.1 without it keep working — the backup state is then reported but not persisted.

docs.title: SQLAlchemy schema notes
docs.text: The passkey_credentials table is unchanged in 0.2 on PostgreSQL and SQLite. On MySQL/MariaDB credential_id is now VARBINARY(1023). Earlier versions declared an unbounded BLOB primary key, so create_all failed on MySQL and no existing MySQL table needs migrating.

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text:
Implement the Protocol against any store, then prove it with the shipped contract suite:

import pytest
from fastapi_passkeys.testing import check_credential_repository, check_challenge_store


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_my_repo():
    await check_credential_repository(MyCredentialRepository)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_my_store():
    await check_challenge_store(lambda clock: MyChallengeStore(clock=clock))

This is exactly how the SQLAlchemy, Redis, and in-memory adapters are tested — so an SQLModel, Tortoise, or Beanie adapter you write is held to the same bar.
